findings.reason: the node's own first case cannot pass as described and the plan states no rule for a receipt id the log does not name, so the worker has to invent one and a symmetric call is what case 3 forbids.
findings.text: §7 requires the first case's refusal to name "the count and the ids" for an `after_suite` arm carrying the first (failing) run's `failure_ids` against a log whose last run passed, while fixing the id comparison's direction as "a bare receipt id matches a qualified log id"; §2's `failure_ids_covered(base_ids, head_ids)` returns only head ids the base fails to cover, so in that direction a passing last run leaves nothing uncovered and only the count is named, and the reverse call that would catch the receipt's extra ids refuses the third case because §2's rule makes a qualified base match "only the same qualified id"

findings.reason: an armed run promoted with an explicit `--gate-log-path` naming a different pytest run is compared across two runs and refused on honest evidence, which is the false-refusal class §1 exists to remove; the plan needs a stated identity condition (arm path or digest equals the cited log) before either comparison, and a rule for an arm that records only a digest.
findings.text: §7 compares the fresh manifest's `after_suite` figures against "the cited log", but a suite arm carries its own `log_path` or `log_digest` (required for an armed promotion by `ledger.suite_observation_missing_fields`, reckon/ledger.py:523–527) and nothing in the check ties the gate check's cited log to that arm
